MATHEMATICS — TERMLY EXAM #8 (TERM 2)
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: MATHEMATICS
TIME ALLOWED: 60 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. A matatu carries m passengers. Eight get in and three get out. Which expression shows the number of passengers now? (1 mark)
   A. 8m − 3
   B. m + 11
   C. m − 5
   D. m + 5

2. Which expression shows "3 times a number a"? (1 mark)
   A. a + 3
   B. a − 3
   C. a ÷ 3
   D. 3a

3. Otieno is a years old. His sister is 3 years older. Which expression shows his sister's age? (1 mark)
   A. 3a
   B. a − 3
   C. a ÷ 3
   D. a + 3

4. A triangle has sides of 3 cm, 4 cm and 5 cm. What is its perimeter? (1 mark)
   A. 12 cm
   B. 13 cm
   C. 7 cm
   D. 14 cm

5. A farmer plants seedlings 50 cm apart. How long is a row with 9 gaps between the seedlings? (1 mark)
   A. 4 m 5 cm
   B. 5 m 50 cm
   C. 4 m 50 cm
   D. 450 m

6. A rectangle is 9 cm long and 4 cm wide. What is its perimeter? (1 mark)
   A. 26 cm
   B. 28 cm
   C. 36 cm
   D. 13 cm

7. A tile is 10 cm long and 10 cm wide. It is covered with 1 cm squares. How many squares fit? (1 mark)
   A. 40
   B. 20
   C. 10
   D. 100

8. A rectangle is made of 6 rows with 6 unit squares in each row. What is its area? (1 mark)
   A. 42 square units
   B. 36 square units
   C. 12 square units
   D. 24 square units

9. A floor is covered with square tiles in 8 rows of 12 tiles. How many tiles are on the floor? (1 mark)
   A. 20 tiles
   B. 86 tiles
   C. 96 tiles
   D. 104 tiles

10. When we stack blocks to make a cuboid, what do we do first? (1 mark)
   A. Count the corners of the room
   B. Make one flat layer with rows and columns
   C. Cut the blocks into halves
   D. Put all the blocks in one long line only

11. A stack of soda crates has 5 crates along a wall, 4 crates deep and 4 layers high. How many crates are in the stack? (1 mark)
   A. 100 crates
   B. 80 crates
   C. 13 crates
   D. 20 crates

12. A cuboid is 7 blocks long, 3 blocks wide and 2 blocks high. What is its volume? (1 mark)
   A. 42 blocks
   B. 12 blocks
   C. 21 blocks
   D. 49 blocks

13. What is 1/2 L + 1/4 L? (1 mark)
   A. 3/4 L
   B. 1 1/4 L
   C. 1/2 L
   D. 1 L

14. A shop sells 3 packets of milk of 1/2 L each. What is the total amount of milk? (1 mark)
   A. 2 L
   B. 1 1/2 L
   C. 3 L
   D. 1 L

15. A tank has 50 L of water and 18 L is used. How much is left? (1 mark)
   A. 22 L
   B. 32 L
   C. 68 L
   D. 42 L

16. What is 6 1/4 kg − 2 1/2 kg? (1 mark)
   A. 4 1/4 kg
   B. 4 kg
   C. 3 3/4 kg
   D. 3 1/2 kg

17. What is 2 1/2 kg + 3/4 kg? (1 mark)
   A. 3 kg
   B. 3 1/4 kg
   C. 3 3/4 kg
   D. 3 1/2 kg

18. A film starts at 4:20 p.m. and lasts 1 hour 40 minutes. At what time does it end? (1 mark)
   A. 5:60 p.m.
   B. 6:00 p.m.
   C. 5:40 p.m.
   D. 6:20 p.m.

19. How many minutes are in 3 hours? (1 mark)
   A. 180 minutes
   B. 72 minutes
   C. 240 minutes
   D. 300 minutes

20. What is 4 h 35 min + 3 h 40 min? (1 mark)
   A. 7 h 15 min
   B. 8 h 15 min
   C. 8 h 25 min
   D. 8 h 5 min

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
21. A vendor sells 2 bags of maize (m) and 3 bags of beans (b) on Monday, and 4 bags of maize and 1 bag of beans on Tuesday. (a) Write an expression for Monday. (b) Write an expression for Tuesday. (c) Simplify the expression for the two days together. (5 marks)

22. Rectangle P has 5 rows and 7 columns. Rectangle Q has 6 rows and 6 columns. Which has the bigger area and by how much? (4 marks)

23. Add 2 hours 45 minutes and 1 hour 30 minutes. (3 marks)

24. Why can we not tell the mass of an object only by looking at its size? Give an example. (3 marks)

25. A school timetable shows assembly from 8:00 a.m. to 8:20 a.m. and mathematics from 8:20 a.m. to 9:10 a.m. Find how long each lasts and the total time. (4 marks)

26. Write 5x + 3y − 2x + y in its simplest form. (3 marks)

27. A hall floor is covered with 12 rows of 15 square tiles. (a) How many tiles cover the floor? (b) A smaller room has 9 rows of 12 tiles. How many more tiles does the hall need than the smaller room? (5 marks)

28. A mother buys 3/4 kg of tomatoes and 1/2 kg of onions. Find the total mass. (3 marks)
pages.answers:
MATHEMATICS — TERMLY EXAM #8 (TERM 2) · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. D — m + 5
   m + 8 − 3 = m + 5.

2. D — 3a
   The key words tell us the operation. "3 times a number a" is written 3a.

3. D — a + 3
   Older means add, so her age is a + 3.

4. A — 12 cm
   Add all three sides: 3 + 4 + 5 = 12 cm.

5. C — 4 m 50 cm
   9 × 50 = 450 cm = 4 m 50 cm.

6. A — 26 cm
   Perimeter = 9 + 4 + 9 + 4 = 26 cm.

7. D — 100
   10 rows × 10 columns = 100 squares.

8. B — 36 square units
   Area = rows × columns = 6 × 6 = 36 square units.

9. C — 96 tiles
   8 × 12 = 96 tiles.

10. B — Make one flat layer with rows and columns
   We build one layer first and then add more layers on top.

11. B — 80 crates
   5 × 4 = 20 crates per layer and 20 × 4 = 80 crates.

12. A — 42 blocks
   One layer has 7 × 3 = 21 blocks. There are 2 layers, so the volume is 21 × 2 = 42 blocks.

13. A — 3/4 L
   Work with the whole litres first and then the parts. 1/2 L + 1/4 L = 3/4 L.

14. B — 1 1/2 L
   3 × 1/2 = 3/2 = 1 1/2 L.

15. B — 32 L
   50 − 18 = 32 L.

16. C — 3 3/4 kg
   Work with the whole kilograms first and then the parts. 6 1/4 kg − 2 1/2 kg = 3 3/4 kg.

17. B — 3 1/4 kg
   Work with the whole kilograms first and then the parts. 2 1/2 kg + 3/4 kg = 3 1/4 kg.

18. B — 6:00 p.m.
   4:20 + 1 hour = 5:20 and 5:20 + 40 minutes = 6:00 p.m.

19. A — 180 minutes
   1 hour = 60 minutes, so 3 × 60 = 180 minutes.

20. B — 8 h 15 min
   Add the minutes and hours, then change 60 minutes into 1 hour. The answer is 8 h 15 min.

SECTION B
----
21. (5 marks)
   Answer: (a) 2m + 3b (b) 4m + b (c) 2m + 3b + 4m + b = 6m + 4b
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for (a), 1 mark for (b), 3 marks for (c): 1 mark for adding the expressions, 1 mark for 6m, 1 mark for 4b.

22. (4 marks)
   Answer: Q is bigger by 1 square unit.
   Working / marking points: P = 35 (1 mark); Q = 36 (1 mark); Q is bigger (1 mark); difference 1 (1 mark).

23. (3 marks)
   Answer: 4 hours 15 minutes
   Working / marking points: 45 + 30 = 75 min and 2 + 1 = 3 h (1 mark); 75 min = 1 h 15 min (1 mark); total 4 h 15 min (1 mark).

24. (3 marks)
   Answer: A large sponge is light but a small stone is heavy. Mass depends on what the object is made of, so we must measure it.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for saying size does not decide mass, 1 mark for an example, 1 mark for saying we must measure.

25. (4 marks)
   Answer: Assembly 20 minutes, mathematics 50 minutes, total 70 minutes (1 hour 10 minutes).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each duration, 1 mark for adding, 1 mark for 1 h 10 min.

26. (3 marks)
   Answer: 3x + 4y
   Working / marking points: x terms: 5x − 2x = 3x (1 mark). y terms: 3y + y = 4y (1 mark). Answer 3x + 4y (1 mark).

27. (5 marks)
   Answer: (a) 180 tiles (b) 72 more tiles
   Working / marking points: (a) 12 × 15: 12 × 10 = 120 and 12 × 5 = 60, so 180 (2 marks); smaller room 9 × 12 = 108 (1 mark); 180 − 108 (1 mark); 72 tiles (1 mark).

28. (3 marks)
   Answer: 1 1/4 kg
   Working / marking points: 3/4 + 1/2 = 3/4 + 2/4 (1 mark); = 5/4 (1 mark); = 1 1/4 kg (1 mark).
